If both ends extend beyond 0 and 1, the uniformly fractional feasible density assigns a proper positive mass on every positive fiber. Replacing any one such assignment by an equal-mass dominated measure on that same fiber keeps both constraints. If the minimum is zero and some base exceeds one, theta M>M-w_0 leaves a proper positive lower trim of the zero fiber. If the maximum is one and some site is negative, 0<theta M<w_1 leaves a proper positive upper trim of the one fiber. No other support case is possible.

For any proper mass s on a full-dimensional fiber, the homothet with factor (s/w_z)^(1/d) and center parameter v in K_z stays inside the fiber. Its indicator has mass s, and its centroid ranges over a translated positive dilation of K_z. Fixing other fiber allocations preserves the two constraints and contributes a fixed vector to the whole centroid, so this range has interior. The complementary map transfers interior to the other body.

For John uniqueness, the feasible center and positive-semidefinite shape parameter set is bounded and closed, and an inscribed ball makes the maximum determinant positive. Averaging distinct maximizing shape matrices would strictly improve log determinant. If they coincide but centers differ, normalize them to unit balls centered at +/-v. The ellipsoid with shape (I+vv^T)^(1/2) is contained in their convex hull by the displayed support inequality and has determinant sqrt(1+||v||^2)>1. Thus the inscribed maximal ellipsoid is unique, including d=1.

The complementary affine map is invertible with nonzero constant Jacobian. It maps inscribed ellipsoids bijectively and multiplies all their volumes by the same factor, so uniqueness identifies the John ellipsoids and transports the centers. Rearranging their affine relation gives the stated weighted center identity.
